title: Outlook on the web: tenant default for using commas to separate recipients
summary: The briefing passes. Microsoft's reference supports the organisation-wide PowerShell control and its documented default, and the roadmap facts match the record. The briefing appropriately leaves the user-preference interaction, Windows applicability and policy-correction completion unresolved.

claims.claim: Administrators can define a tenant-wide default for whether commas separate recipients in the Outlook on the web Mail Compose and Reply setting.
claims.quote: Admins will be able to define a tenant-wide default value for the Mail Compose and Reply setting that controls whether commas are used to separate recipients.

claims.where: controls[0].api; summary; What's changing; Governance guidance; Governance controls
claims.claim: Exchange PowerShell provides Set-OrganizationConfig -RecipientDelimiters $false to set the organisation-wide default so commas do not separate recipients.
claims.quote: The RecipientDelimiters parameter specifies the organization-wide default for the Mail Compose and Reply setting that controls whether commas are used to separate recipients.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Scope
claims.claim: RecipientDelimiters is available only in the cloud-based Exchange service.
claims.quote:
Applicable: Exchange Online
This parameter is available only in the cloud-based service.

claims.where: controls[0].note; What's changing; Why it matters; rationale: risk
claims.claim: The parameter description says $true uses commas to separate recipients by default and is the default value.
claims.quote: $true: Commas are used to separate recipients by default. This value is the default.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Security & identity; Governance guidance
claims.claim: Setting RecipientDelimiters to $false means commas are not used to separate recipients by default.
claims.quote: $false: Commas aren't used to separate recipients by default.

claims.where: What's changing
claims.claim: The cited release notes say Outlook Web and the New Outlook support semicolons or commas as recipient separators by default.
claims.quote: By default, Outlook Web and the New Outlook support separating recipients by using either a semicolon or a comma.

claims.where: What's changing; Risk assessment: Change & support; Governance controls
claims.claim: The user setting lets individuals choose whether a comma separates recipients or forms part of a contact name.
claims.quote: This new setting allows users to choose if the comma should be used as a recipient separator or instead allowed as part of the contact name.

claims.where: Why it matters; Governance guidance: Before rollout
claims.claim: Microsoft identifies contacts formatted as Family name, First name as a use case for this setting.
claims.quote: This is helpful for organizations where contacts follow the "Family name, First name" format.
